name: Ray's Western Wear & Saddlery
old_description: Exceptional fit, built-in stretch, and dependable durability.
about:
Ray's Western Wear & Saddlery operates from Oacoma, South Dakota, a location it has occupied since 1996 when the business moved to capture Interstate 90 traffic. The company traces its roots to April 1957, when Ray Steckelberg purchased a men's clothing store in nearby Chamberlain and began selling horse tack from the basement. The Steckelberg family has retained ownership across four generations; today the store is led by great‑granddaughter Brooke and her husband Kaiden, continuing a legacy that spans more than 65 years.

The store functions as a full‑line western retailer, stocking a wide assortment of boots, denim, seasonal apparel, and equestrian tack. Its sales floor emphasizes boot variety — marketed as the largest selection in the state — and includes a dedicated tack room where saddle and horse‑fitting services are offered. Brands carried include Ariat footwear and apparel, as well as specialty items such as SoGlo grooming tape. The operation runs from a single retail location; no manufacturing or wholesale distribution is described.

Customers range from local ranchers and rodeo competitors to travelers pulling horse trailers along I‑90. The business serves the western lifestyle market, supplying both work‑oriented gear and fashion‑forward seasonal collections. Its client base spans the broader equestrian community and general consumers seeking durable western wear.

The company positions itself as "South Dakota's Cowboy Store," highlighting its family heritage, personalized fitting expertise, and a product mix built on fit, stretch, and durability. The transition from a basement tack operation to a destination retail outlet reflects a deliberate focus on serving the region's horse and ranch culture.
